items.name: Delivery
items.basis: manage_files save writes via COM Document.SaveAs and returns a path. Executed: P9 save|plan.dwg reported path <out>/plan.dwg while SaveAs wrote <out>/drawings/plan.dwg; P10 dxf/pdf reported path <out>/plan2 (no extension; file does not exist) while SaveAs got <out>/drawings/plan2.dxf|.pdf with no type argument; P11a/P12 relative and absolute paths reported verbatim while the file was written under <out>/drawings/; P15 dashboard switch_drawing to a nonexistent drawing returned success=true.
items.scope_and_limits: Serious false success (source-demonstrated): files.py _save reports path=output_dir/filename (or the caller's filepath), while file_mixin actually saves to output_dir/drawings/<name>.<format> (resolve_export_path adds the 'drawings' subfolder and an extension), so the returned path can name a file that was not written. format=dxf/pdf only changes the filename extension; SaveAs is called without SaveAsType and PDF has no plot path, yet the op reports 'Drawing saved'. No readback, hashes, version or per-format scope. No committed results, logs of tool calls, benchmarks or completed test CI exist for this commit or its ancestors (only gh-pages deployment runs 23094624408/23107086677, which build docs). Without output/behavioral evidence the anchor caps this item at 1. Serious false-success reproduced at the tool layer (independent of COM). What AutoCAD writes for a .pdf/.dxf name without a SaveAs type is COM-only and not executed. Remains 1 (cap 2 has no effect).

deduction.reason: Withhold 4: no delivery gate/readback; reported save path/format reproduced as false (cap 2); no real-backend output.

items.name: Backend contract
items.basis: One COM adapter parameterised by ProgID for AutoCAD, ZWCAD, GstarCAD and BricsCAD; manage_session offers list_supported, check_running, connect/status; lazy connection with auto-detection. Executed: the product's src/server.py ran as a real stdio MCP subprocess (transport auto-detected) and listed 7 tools; manage_session list_supported returned autocad/zwcad/gcad/bricscad; with no CAD reachable, draw_entities returned 'Could not connect to any supported CAD application' (no false success). On Linux without pywin32 the package refuses at import with 'AutoCAD adapter requires Windows OS with COM support'.
items.scope_and_limits: No per-backend capability map (e.g. _AIMLEADEREDITADD and PNGOUT command strings are sent to every backend); missing pywin32 or an absent CAD surfaces as a generic error. No committed results, logs of tool calls, benchmarks or completed test CI exist for this commit or its ancestors (only gh-pages deployment runs 23094624408/23107086677, which build docs). deduction.reason: Withhold 3: capability boundaries per backend undeclared; no cross-backend postcondition evidence.

declared_contract: A Windows-only Python MCP server (FastMCP, v0.2.0) that drives a running AutoCAD, ZWCAD, GstarCAD or BricsCAD over COM (pywin32) through seven shorthand batch tools: drawing primitives/dimensions/leaders/tables, layers, entity selection and transforms, blocks and attributes, file new/save(dwg/dxf/pdf)/close/switch, session/view/undo/screenshot, and entity data export to JSON/Excel, plus a local web dashboard. No headless/DXF backend and no domain or engineering-standards workflows are claimed.

serious_defects.description: manage_files save reports a path that was not written (output_dir/filename or the caller's path vs actual output_dir/drawings/<name>.<fmt>); dxf/pdf only change the extension (SaveAs called with one argument) and the op reports 'Drawing saved'. Reproduced at the tool layer (P9, P10, P11a, P12).
move/rotate/scale return success=true with count=len(handles) when only some handles were transformed. Reproduced (P4).

Shipped config.json sets allow_arbitrary_paths=true: absolute paths outside the output dir are written (P11b) and the repo's own traversal test fails. HTTP mode accepts unauthenticated MCP initialize, including with a foreign Host/Origin (P16).
Dashboard POST /api/cad/switch_drawing ignores the adapter's False result and returns success=true for a nonexistent drawing (new in strict pass, P15).

limitations: Probes ran the product's real tool, parser, adapter and server code, but against a reviewer-written in-memory fake COM document; they show what the product reports and passes to COM, not what a CAD application does.
The test-suite pass counts required a reviewer pywin32-stub plugin (probes/win32shim.py); as shipped on Linux the suite cannot collect.
The fake model in probe_results.json for P1 is serialised after later probes mutated it; P1's pass verdict was computed at call time.
COM-only behaviour stays at first-pass evidence level.
Published scores of this repository (including U-C4N's) were not consulted.
